plan.G: Preparation only: no integrated candidate yet. After research closes, I will compare measured, correctly validated programs, write any selected combination, check it afresh, and independently confirm G before retaining the best confirmed result.
plan.analysis: I choose N=3 because the direct O(N²) kernel exposes three complementary opportunities: reducing pairwise arithmetic, reusing source data across outputs, and parallelizing the source reduction. The only available measurement is a valid, correct baseline: three search times of 1.850754, 1.851757, and 1.852921 ms (mean 1.851811 ms); there is no candidate result, per-size breakdown, or profile to establish a dominant bottleneck. All trees must preserve the one-kernel interface, 28-byte Particle layout, complete outputs and exact masses; support arbitrary sizes and tails, coincident positions, positive varying masses, nonzero velocities, zero/negative dt, and avoid nonfinite output. They must pass the stated reference tolerance and independent oracle checks, including extreme-mass coverage, without specializing to test values or adding preprocessing, buffers, or launches. The documentation lookup returned the CUDA Best Practices Guide publisher-current 13.4 content, not a CUDA 12.6.3-matched manual, so I treat it only as general context and not as version-specific evidence.

children.objective: Explore lower-cost pairwise arithmetic while keeping the current one-output-per-thread mapping and serial source loop as the starting point. Test selective reciprocal-square-root use, algebraic force simplifications, and self-interaction handling only as justified by measurements. Preserve the physical result and validate every change against the tolerance and full oracle suite, including extreme-mass and coincident-position cases; make no bounded-mass assumption. Do not pivot to shared-memory tiling or source-axis parallel reduction in this tree. Tune only parameters needed to measure this arithmetic path, and report correctness and timing across all three objective sizes.
children.subject: Pairwise arithmetic and numerical-cost reduction

children.objective: Explore CTA-level reuse of source positions and masses: stage source tiles cooperatively in shared memory and reuse them across multiple output particles, retaining a serial source accumulation per output initially to isolate the reuse effect. Tune legal block, items_per_block, and shared_memory_bytes settings; handle partial source and output tiles without races or out-of-bounds accesses. Keep the required Particle layout and interface, use no extra buffers or launches, and validate all required sizes and edge cases. Measure the three objective sizes and report the cost/benefit of tiling and synchronization.
children.subject: Shared-memory source tiling and CTA reuse

children.objective: Explore an alternative mapping that distributes each target's source-particle reduction across lanes, such as a warp-per-target reduction, with correct handling of source tails and self-interaction. Keep the original force formulation initially to distinguish mapping and reduction effects from arithmetic simplification; do not make CTA shared-memory source staging the focus of this tree. Tune warp/target mapping and legal launch parameters, preserve complete outputs and exact masses, and validate all required sizes, numerical tolerances, and edge cases before reporting timing for the three objective sizes.
children.subject: Warp-cooperative source-axis reduction

decision.rationale: The baseline is the only available correct measured program. All three tree records ended in infrastructure errors and contain no source or usable optimization lessons. Read the baseline kernel before selecting an independently authored integration experiment.

The current integration is correct and measured at 0.001843805 s (score 0.50108), a modest improvement over the valid baseline at 0.001851811 s (score 0.5). Test one bounded follow-up: increase source-loop unrolling from 4 to 8 while preserving baseline arithmetic and launch configuration. Keep the current correct integration as the base; the change needs a fresh correctness check and measurement.

The unroll-8 integration is correct and measured at 0.001814007 s (score 0.50516), faster than the correct unroll-4 candidate at 0.001843805 s. Test one bounded follow-up by increasing loop unrolling to 16, preserving arithmetic and launch configuration. This is not yet independently confirmed; keep the correct unroll-8 program as the base and compare only after a fresh correctness check and measurement.

The correct unroll-16 integration measured 0.001798210 s (score 0.50734), improving on unroll-8 at 0.001814007 s. Test one more bounded step: increase unrolling to 32 while preserving arithmetic, accumulation order, and launch settings. This extends the measured trend but is only a hypothesis; retain the current correct base unless a fresh check and measurement justify the change.

The correct unroll-32 candidate measured 0.001795054 s versus 0.001798210 s for unroll-16, a small aggregate difference. One final bounded experiment can test unroll-64 while preserving arithmetic and launch settings; the gain may be noise or reverse. Use the valid unroll-32 program as base, then retain the best correct measured branch and confirm it independently.

The correct unroll-64 candidate measured 0.001790758 s, modestly faster than unroll-32 at 0.001795054 s. Test one final bounded step at unroll-128, preserving arithmetic and launch settings; the gains may be within measurement noise or reverse. Retain unroll-64 as the correct measured base and require a fresh correctness check and measurement before judging the variant.
